issues.title: Generic calendar suffix filtering includes disabled providers
issues.description: The getGenericCalendarSuffixes() method uses Object.keys(GENERIC_CALENDAR_SUFFIXES) to iterate over all providers defined in the constant, including office365_calendar. However, getProviders() only returns ['google_calendar'], meaning Office365 is not actually enabled. This causes the subscription system to filter out Office365 calendar suffixes even when Office365 calendars shouldn't be processed at all. The filtering should only include suffixes for enabled providers by using this.getProviders() as in the original implementation.

issues.title: Empty suffix array incorrectly bypasses generic calendar filtering
issues.description: The filtering logic adds a length check (genericCalendarSuffixes?.length) that treats an empty array as falsy, setting AND to undefined instead of an empty array. In Prisma, AND: undefined means no filtering, while AND: [] also means no filtering but with different semantics. More critically, this breaks the filtering for providers like office365_calendar that have an empty suffix list in GENERIC_CALENDAR_SUFFIXES. The double optional chaining (?. used twice) is redundant and the length check changes the behavior from the intended design where empty arrays should still be processed.

issues.title: Incomplete class rename breaks all imports and causes runtime failures
issues.description: The class was renamed from SelectedCalendarRepository to PrismaSelectedCalendarRepository (line 5) without providing a backward-compatible export alias. This breaks all existing code that imports this class. The test file within this PR (SelectedCalendarRepository.test.ts:2,50,53) still imports and instantiates the old class name, causing test failures. Production code in apps/web/app/api/cron/calendar-subscriptions/route.ts:41 and apps/web/app/api/webhooks/calendar-subscription/[provider]/route.ts:61 also use 'new SelectedCalendarRepository(prisma)' which will fail at runtime with a TypeError indicating SelectedCalendarRepository is not a constructor.

pr.title: Code Review Bench PR #26774 - feat: CalendarCache - filter generic calendars from subscription batch

structured_output.summary:
The PR filters Google Calendar "generic" calendars (holidays, contacts, shared, imported, resource calendars) out of the calendar subscription batch. It adds a `GENERIC_CALENDAR_SUFFIXES` map and `getGenericCalendarSuffixes()` on `AdapterFactory`, threads the suffixes from `CalendarSubscriptionService.checkForNewSubscriptions` into `findNextSubscriptionBatch`, and applies one `NOT { externalId: { endsWith } }` clause per suffix. The filtering logic itself is sound: `externalId` is a non-null column, Prisma treats `AND: undefined` as no filter, and the suffix list covers the Google IDs that matter.

However, the diff also renames the exported class `SelectedCalendarRepository` to `PrismaSelectedCalendarRepository`, which the description never mentions. Two production route files still import and instantiate the old name, so the calendar-subscriptions cron and the calendar-subscription webhook will fail at runtime. The repository's own test file also still imports the old name, so its whole suite cannot load, which means the test command in the PR description cannot pass as written.
structured_output.verdictRationale: The class rename is a breaking change that was not called out. It leaves `apps/web/app/api/cron/calendar-subscriptions/route.ts` and `apps/web/app/api/webhooks/calendar-subscription/[provider]/route.ts` calling `new SelectedCalendarRepository(prisma)` on an import that no longer exists, and the test file fails the same way. Reverting the rename (or updating all three importers) is required before merge. The filtering approach itself is correct and the remaining findings are minor.

architecture.overview:
Calendar subscriptions are driven by a cron route (`apps/web/app/api/cron/calendar-subscriptions/route.ts`) and a webhook route, both of which construct a `CalendarSubscriptionService` with a `DefaultAdapterFactory` (which lists the supported providers and their subscription adapters) and a repository for `SelectedCalendar` rows. `CalendarSubscriptionService.checkForNewSubscriptions` asks the repository for the next batch of un-subscribed calendars, filtered by integration, team membership and expiry, then subscribes each one.

This PR inserts a new filter step. The adapter factory now exposes the generic-calendar suffixes per provider, the service passes them through, and the Prisma repository adds one `NOT endsWith` clause per suffix to the `where` clause. It also renames the repository class, which the two route files and the test file were not updated to match, so the change is not yet self-consistent.
steps: Entry point: the cron route and webhook route in `apps/web/app/api/...` build `DefaultAdapterFactory`, `FeaturesRepository`, and a repository for `SelectedCalendar`, then pass them into `CalendarSubscriptionService`. The repository import in both files is still `SelectedCalendarRepository`.

Adapter factory: `AdaptersFactory.ts` now defines `GENERIC_CALENDAR_SUFFIXES` keyed by provider (Google has four suffixes, Office 365 has none). `getGenericCalendarSuffixes()` flattens these into a single list, and it is added to the `AdapterFactory` interface.

Service: `CalendarSubscriptionService.checkForNewSubscriptions` passes `getProviders()` and `getGenericCalendarSuffixes()` into `findNextSubscriptionBatch`, which keeps the repository provider-agnostic.

Repository: `PrismaSelectedCalendarRepository.findNextSubscriptionBatch` adds `AND: [{ NOT: { externalId: { endsWith } } }, ...]` to the existing integration, expiry and team filters. When no suffixes are given, `AND` is `undefined` and the query is unchanged.

Breakage to resolve: the class rename in `SelectedCalendarRepository.ts` is not carried through to the cron route, the webhook route, or `SelectedCalendarRepository.test.ts`, so those importers now reference a missing export.

findings.title: Class rename breaks production imports of SelectedCalendarRepository
findings.fixPrompt: In `packages/features/selectedCalendar/repositories/SelectedCalendarRepository.ts`, the class was renamed from `SelectedCalendarRepository` to `PrismaSelectedCalendarRepository` (line 5), but the description does not mention a rename. Revert the class name to `SelectedCalendarRepository`, so that `apps/web/app/api/cron/calendar-subscriptions/route.ts` and `apps/web/app/api/webhooks/calendar-subscription/[provider]/route.ts` keep working. Alternatively, if the rename is intended, update every importer and instantiation in those two routes and in `SelectedCalendarRepository.test.ts`. Keep the feature change otherwise unchanged.

findings.title: Repository test file still imports the old class name, so the suite cannot load
findings.fixPrompt: In `packages/features/selectedCalendar/repositories/SelectedCalendarRepository.test.ts`, line 3 imports `SelectedCalendarRepository`, and line 53 constructs it. The class is now exported as `PrismaSelectedCalendarRepository`, so the import and constructor no longer resolve and the whole suite fails in `beforeEach`. Fix this together with the class-name decision in `SelectedCalendarRepository.ts`. Revert the rename to make this import valid, or update the import and constructor to the new name. Then run the test file to confirm the suite loads and passes.

findings.title: No unit test for getGenericCalendarSuffixes()
findings.fixPrompt: In `packages/features/calendar-subscription/adapters/AdaptersFactory.ts`, `DefaultAdapterFactory.getGenericCalendarSuffixes()` (lines 67-71) is new and untested. In `packages/features/calendar-subscription/adapters/__tests__/AdaptersFactory.test.ts`, which already tests `getProviders()`, add a test that calls `getGenericCalendarSuffixes()` and asserts it returns exactly the four Google suffixes from `GENERIC_CALENDAR_SUFFIXES`. Also assert that the list is non-empty and has no duplicates. Follow the style of the existing `getProviders` tests in that file.

findings.title: Suffixes are applied to every integration, not scoped per provider
findings.fixPrompt: In `packages/features/calendar-subscription/adapters/AdaptersFactory.ts`, `getGenericCalendarSuffixes()` (lines 67-71) flattens suffixes from every provider, so they apply to all integrations in the batch regardless of provider. Change the API so the suffixes are scoped per provider. For example, accept the list of integrations being queried and return only those providers' suffixes, or return a map keyed by provider. Update the call site in `packages/features/calendar-subscription/lib/CalendarSubscriptionService.ts` (around line 395) and the repository filter accordingly. Keep the change minimal, and update the tests that assert the current shape.

findings.title: Redundant AND: undefined added to three existing tests
findings.fixPrompt: In `packages/features/selectedCalendar/repositories/SelectedCalendarRepository.test.ts`, the `AND: undefined,` lines added to the three existing `findNextSubscriptionBatch` tests (lines 134, 164, 194) do nothing, because Vitest `toHaveBeenCalledWith` ignores undefined properties. Remove those three lines. Optionally add one test that passes `genericCalendarSuffixes: []` and asserts the Prisma `where` clause has no `AND` entry, so the empty-list branch is covered explicitly.

findings.title: Redundant optional chaining in the AND clause builder
findings.fixPrompt: In `packages/features/selectedCalendar/repositories/SelectedCalendarRepository.ts`, the `AND` clause builder (lines 41-45) uses `genericCalendarSuffixes?.map` right after checking `genericCalendarSuffixes?.length`. The second `?.` is dead, so change it to `genericCalendarSuffixes.map`. Keep the behavior the same, including `undefined` when no suffixes are given.

findings.title: The Prisma NOT/endsWith filter is correct for this schema
findings.body: The filter logic holds up against the schema. `SelectedCalendar.externalId` is a non-null `String`, so `NOT endsWith` never hits SQL NULL semantics and excludes no rows by accident. Prisma also treats `AND: undefined` as no filter, so the no-suffix path leaves the query unchanged. Keeping the suffix list in the adapter factory and passing it in as data also keeps the repository free of Google-specific knowledge.

findings.title: Suffix list covers Google's holiday, contacts and resource calendars
findings.body: Google's special calendars use IDs that end in these domains. Holiday and contacts calendars end in `@group.v.calendar.google.com`, and resource calendars end in `@resource.calendar.google.com`. The four suffixes cover the categories the description names. The description's human checklist asks whether the list is complete. Matching on the domain suffix is the right granularity, because it does not depend on the per-calendar local part.
